reason: Section 3 declares Crown ownership of bituminous shale substances and makes existing licence agreements subject to the Act and regulations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Crown ownership of bituminous shale rights
proposedGroups.reason: Section 3 declares Crown ownership of bituminous shale substances and makes existing licence agreements subject to the Act and regulations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how section 3 vests bituminous shale rights in the Crown and treats prior licence agreements.

reason: Section 4 bars exploration, evaluation drilling, and mining or production unless the person holds the specified licence, permit, or lease.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Required authorization for bituminous shale exploration and development
proposedGroups.reason: Section 4 bars exploration, evaluation drilling, and mining or production unless the person holds the specified licence, permit, or lease.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which licences, permits, or leases are required before exploring, drilling, mining, producing, or developing bituminous shale.

reason: Section 5 applies Oil and Natural Gas Act well-drilling rules to bituminous shale evaluation wells, while allowing the Minister to vary requirements when conditions warrant.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Evaluation well rules and Minister variation
proposedGroups.reason: Section 5 applies Oil and Natural Gas Act well-drilling rules to bituminous shale evaluation wells, while allowing the Minister to vary requirements when conditions warrant.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what drilling rules apply to bituminous shale evaluation wells and when the Minister may vary them.

reason: Section 6 allows authorized persons to access, enter, inspect, sample, test, and examine bituminous shale locations, equipment, mines, records, and related places.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Authorized access and inspection powers

evidenceText: may have access to all locations, equipment, mines and records
may take samples or carry out any tests

proposedGroups.reason: Section 6 allows authorized persons to access, enter, inspect, sample, test, and examine bituminous shale locations, equipment, mines, records, and related places.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the access, inspection, sampling, testing, and examination powers of persons authorized to enforce the Act.

reason: Section 7 prohibits specified provincial employees from holding monetary interests in bituminous shale property or businesses and creates an offence plus forfeiture of office.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Employee conflict-of-interest prohibition and offence
proposedGroups.reason: Section 7 prohibits specified provincial employees from holding monetary interests in bituminous shale property or businesses and creates an offence plus forfeiture of office.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the monetary-interest prohibition for employees administering the Act and the consequences for violating it.

reason: Section 8 requires a court order for summons or production and prohibits disclosure of certified non-public-interest information.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court orders for official evidence and confidentiality
proposedGroups.reason: Section 8 requires a court order for summons or production and prohibits disclosure of certified non-public-interest information.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister or employees can be compelled to attend or produce documents and when official information may not be disclosed.

reason: Section 9 allows entry and exploration for bituminous shale on Crown lands only with Minister consent and on prescribed terms and conditions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister consent for Crown land exploration

evidenceText: Crown lands may be entered upon and explored
with the consent of the Minister

proposedGroups.reason: Section 9 allows entry and exploration for bituminous shale on Crown lands only with Minister consent and on prescribed terms and conditions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the consent and terms required to enter Crown lands for bituminous shale exploration.

reason: Section 10 separates the right to enter non-Crown land, the surface-use right for authorized holders, and compensation for Crown and non-Crown land damage.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Right to enter non-Crown land
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections state how authorized holders obtain entry to non-Crown land and the surface-use right within their areas.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a bituminous shale authorization holder obtains entry and surface use on land other than Crown land.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Compensation for entry or operations damage
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address compensation for Crown land and private land entry or operations damage.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who is owed compensation for loss or damage caused by bituminous shale entry or operations and how disputes are determined.

reason: Section 11 contains a special-order application process, notice and hearing timing, Minister discretion, compensation referral, security, and substituted service.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Special order application, notice, and hearing
proposedGroups.reason: The first three subsections establish the application, pre-application notice, hearing timing, and Minister decision on a special entry order.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how an authorization holder applies for a special order to enter and use private land.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Compensation, security, and substituted service for special orders
proposedGroups.reason: The final subsections cover compensation determination, the order effective date, security for compensation, and substituted service.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the compensation, security, effective-date, and substituted-service rules for special entry orders.

reason: Section 12 applies Oil and Natural Gas Act rules and prohibits interference with mining, mineral, oil, or gas right holders.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Geophysical exploration rules and non-interference
proposedGroups.reason: Section 12 applies Oil and Natural Gas Act rules and prohibits interference with mining, mineral, oil, or gas right holders.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what rules govern bituminous shale geophysical exploration and whose operations must not be interfered with.

reason: Section 13 authorizes the Minister to grant licences, prohibits overlapping licences or permits or leases, and requires tenders before grant.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Licence to search grant, overlap limits, and tenders
proposedGroups.reason: Section 13 authorizes the Minister to grant licences, prohibits overlapping licences or permits or leases, and requires tenders before grant.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a licence to search is granted, what area conflicts prevent it, and when tenders must be called.

reason: Section 14 sets maximum, minimum, boundary-adjacent, and absolute minimum sizes for a licence area.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Licence area size limits

evidenceText: shall not be less than twenty-five sections
less than one-half of a section

proposedGroups.reason: Section 14 sets maximum, minimum, boundary-adjacent, and absolute minimum sizes for a licence area.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the maximum and minimum size limits for a bituminous shale licence area.

reason: Section 15 sets the initial three-year term, two annual renewals, and written renewal application deadline with fee and deposit.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Licence to search term and renewal application
proposedGroups.reason: Section 15 sets the initial three-year term, two annual renewals, and written renewal application deadline with fee and deposit.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the term, renewal limit, and renewal application requirements for a licence to search.

reason: Section 16 requires annual exploratory work, an initial deposit, and maintained deposits for renewals.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Licence to search work deposits
proposedGroups.reason: Section 16 requires annual exploratory work, an initial deposit, and maintained deposits for renewals.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the exploratory work and deposit requirements for a licence to search.

reason: Section 17 covers applying for and selecting a development permit area, Minister grant authority, expiry of the licence to search, and permit term and renewal.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development permit application, area, and grant
proposedGroups.reason: The first three subsections address who applies, what area is selected, and how the Minister grants a development permit.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a licensee applies for and receives a bituminous shale development permit.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development permit effect, term, and renewal
proposedGroups.reason: The final subsections state the effect on the licence to search and the development permit term and renewal requirements.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a development permit affects the licence to search and how permit renewal works.

reason: Section 17.1 requires annual development work, an initial deposit, and maintained deposits for development permit renewals.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Development permit work deposits
proposedGroups.reason: Section 17.1 requires annual development work, an initial deposit, and maintained deposits for development permit renewals.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the development work and deposit requirements for a development permit.

reason: Section 18 separates the lease application and area determination process from the effect of granting a lease and the transitional deeming rule for earlier leases.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Conversion from development permit to lease
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections govern applying for a lease, determining the lease area, granting the lease, and expiry of the development permit.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a permittee converts a development permit to a bituminous shale lease.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Earlier leases deemed development permits
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 18(5) is a distinct transitional deeming rule for earlier leases.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how leases granted before September 1, 1981 are deemed under section 18.

reason: Section 19 allows the Minister to grant leases to permittees and approve transfers to another lessee with minimum area and new lease consequences.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Crown land leases and lease-area transfers
proposedGroups.reason: Section 19 allows the Minister to grant leases to permittees and approve transfers to another lessee with minimum area and new lease consequences.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how Crown land bituminous shale leases are granted and how lease area transfers are approved.
